The advice was local, concise, and more valuable than the chart's polished polygon.

Gabriel caught the marks. Engine pressure fell below warning. He reduced load and lost a degree of heading. Surf advanced across the bow.

"Two minutes," Els said.

They secured watertight doors, stopped fuel transfer, closed tank vents to collision state, and moved everyone clear of the forecast impact path. Lotte lay strapped on a stretcher behind the bridge seats, issuing no sentimental farewell to her vessel. Tomasz knelt beside her and held the splint.

At five meters depth Gabriel aimed for the center of the inlet. The fish finder showed a smooth rise, then a sharp irregularity to port. He corrected starboard. The dome shifted right.

"Too far," Pawlu said on radio. "Five degrees left."

Gabriel amended. The engine coughed.

At four meters under the sounder, less than a meter beneath the keel, he put the rudder amidships. Momentum would carry them. He ordered nothing. Els ordered engine stop, fuel shutoff, and all hands brace.

The propeller ceased.

`Nkem` entered surf bow first. The first contact was a shudder under the forefoot, not a collision. Sand slowed them. A second wave lifted the stern and drove the hull farther onto the shelf. The vessel heeled six degrees to port, recovered to three, and stopped. Loose tools jumped despite lashings. A cabinet opened. Somewhere aft, glass broke.

No tank alarm sounded.

For several seconds Gabriel kept his hands on dead controls. He had spent years treating preservation of this steel hull as the continuity beneath every compromise. Now he had intentionally used the hull as an instrument to save the lives inside it.

"Engine secured," Marcin reported. "No fire. Bilge alarm in aft steering flat. Checking."

Els took the con back formally. "Grounding complete, position—"

She read coordinates. The time was 07:49.

The rescue began without waiting for interpretation. The vessel rested on sand with surf striking the starboard quarter. Pawlu's fishing boat entered from the east and found a calmer approach. The patrol deployed an inflatable rescue craft. Because `Nkem` was stable for the moment, they evacuated Lotte first with the medic. Her wrist injury and scalp wound required hospital imaging; she remained conscious. Two crew with bruises followed. No one was unscathed in the colloquial sense, but no one had life-threatening trauma.

Marcin found seawater entering around a damaged stern-tube seal at a manageable rate. The propeller had likely touched sand and perhaps the edge of shale. Portable pumps controlled the ingress. Fuel tanks remained intact. An iridescent streak near the stern proved to be less than a liter of hydraulic oil from a deck fitting; booms were deployed and the environmental officer notified.

The certified evidence case was already ashore in court custody. Anthea sent confirmation from the police pier that she would depart commercially if permitted. Still, the ship carried operational comparison notes and public copies relevant to Athens. Els authorized their transfer to Pawlu's boat under a fresh manifest, together with the crew committee minutes and sabotage photographs copied by the patrol officer. Originals remained in their repositories. Pawlu would deliver the sealed pouch to a government quay, where a Greek diplomatic courier could collect it.

The fisherman accepted no heroic role. "I am going to the quay because my catch is there," he said. "The pouch can accompany the fish."

By 09:12 all nonessential personnel were ashore. Gabriel, Els, Marcin, a salvage officer, and two crew remained aboard to stabilize systems. Lotte's last order before the rescue craft took her was that Gabriel not stay merely because he owned the vessel. He stayed because Marcin requested mechanical assistance and the salvage officer approved.

The storm eased enough to reveal land. The coast was close and shockingly ordinary: low buildings, a road, wet scrub, pale shelves. `Nkem` had stopped within the sand lens, bow elevated, stern afloat. Had they drifted two hundred meters north, the hull would have met rock. Had Gabriel held five degrees south, they would have crossed dense seagrass and likely rolled against a reef. The margin did not become evidence of superiority. It showed how much rescue had depended on Pawlu's marks, the environmental officer's knowledge, Marcin's improvised fuel, Els's authority, Lotte's decision, and weather that had spared one final minute.

Police boarded at 10:03. They treated the fuel system as a potential crime scene. Marcin surrendered no tools until each was distinguished from preexisting equipment. The reversed locking wire, broken paint line, contaminated filters, samples, temporary bypass, and day-tank contents were photographed and sealed. The survey and fueling records were obtained from Marseille. Harbor Control logs preserved every order and refusal.

An investigator asked Gabriel why he had not surrendered the vessel when ordered.

"Surrender to whom?"

"Harbor Control and patrol authority."

"We accepted patrol boarding, tug assistance, and eventual evacuation. We did not stop propulsion while transfer capacity was insufficient and rock lay downwind. Lotte Okafor—Captain de Vries—"

The mistake caught him. Lotte was not an extension of his family or ship. "Captain de Vries retained command until injury. Els Vermeer then commanded. I handled the vessel under emergency direction."

"You chose to ground."

"I recommended the sand shelf before the injury. Captain de Vries selected it. Chief Mate Vermeer directed the approach and appointed me to the controls under necessity. I executed it."

The investigator looked dissatisfied by the distribution of agency. Legal accounts preferred a villain or rescuer with both hands on the wheel. Reality had been less tidy.

At noon a salvage survey found deformation at the forefoot, probable propeller and shaft damage, flooding in the steering flat, and abrasion along the port bilge keel. Refloating before sea conditions moderated could worsen damage. Repair estimates would begin with underwater inspection. The vessel was immobilized for days at minimum and perhaps beyond economic repair. Her lender, insurer, crew, charterer, environmental authority, and Maltese court all had claims on what happened next.

Gabriel sat on the wet afterdeck while Marcin made tea in a saucepan because the galley kettle had broken. Weariness arrived as a physical weight behind his ribs. He expected grief to resemble a torn cable. Instead it seeped into every arrangement: the familiar deck angle changed, the engine silent, sand grinding softly beneath the hull with each swell.

"You can say it," Marcin told him.

"Say what?"

"That you saved her by wrecking her. Owners enjoy contraposition."

"We saved people. We may have reduced damage by choosing sand. The ship is not a person who consented to a noble injury."

Marcin handed him a mug. "Better. Less orotund."

At 13:38 Mira called from Valletta. Lotte had a displaced wrist fracture, three scalp sutures, and no intracranial bleeding on initial imaging. She would remain under observation because of the head strike. The evidence package had left Malta on a Greek government flight after the court rejected an emergency Harborlight application to detain it. Noor and Elena remained for interviews. Mira had secured seats to Athens for the next morning if release conditions allowed.

"Anagnostou will convene delegations tomorrow afternoon," Mira said. "She has not delayed ratification."

"Then go."

"What about you?"

He looked along `Nkem`'s rail toward the fishing boat returning with empty crates. "I remain for the casualty inquiry. My movement order does not let me leave, and someone must answer for the grounding."

"You did not command until necessity."

"I still acted. That is not a complaint."

He heard her understand the distinction because it was one she had begun to make about Alexandria.

At 15:06 police found the source of the grey emulsifier. It was a commercial spill-response compound designed to keep water and particulates suspended long enough to pass through filters. A half-empty sachet lay inside a void behind the day-tank access ladder, wiped but not clean. The compound was not part of `Nkem`'s stores. Yard cameras showed a man in survey coveralls entering the engine-room access during fueling, using a temporary vendor badge linked to Mediterranean Recovery Systems. His face remained hidden. The badge certificate traced to the same contractor group as the cable-chamber cut.

Rell remained an inference, not a verified actor. The shared certificate chain made collusion or common credential access increasingly likely. It did not prove Vale's instruction or convert every Harborlight employee into a villain.

Harbor Control rescinded its northern holding order after the fact and classified the event as machinery casualty under investigation. It did not concede that the initial denial of entry was improper. The infrastructure prosecutor issued no new charge against the crew but reserved offences involving disobedience, environmental damage, and unauthorized command. Gabriel's certificate suspension would complicate the inquiry even under necessity.

At dusk the sea slackened. Divers entered from Pawlu's boat. Their video showed the bow embedded in sand, bilge keel scraped, propeller blades bent, and one shaft bearing displaced. No hull penetration appeared near fuel tanks. Seagrass damage was limited to a narrow prop-wash edge before the engine stopped. The environmental officer called the choice defensible and still required restoration assessment.

Els returned from shore after giving her statement. She stood beside Gabriel at the rail.

"Lotte says you are not to turn the grounding into an obituary," she said.

"I had not intended to eulogize steel."

"You have eulogized the vessel while she was afloat for three years."

That was true. He had made `Nkem` emblematic of independence until every debt, lie, and act of care became an argument about keeping her. Grounded, she existed without the mythology. A working vessel damaged in service. An encumbered asset. A home to a crew that now governed itself. A possible repair. A possible total loss.

"You had command," he said. "I should have said that more clearly to police."

"You corrected yourself. The transcript will show both."

"Would you have chosen the shelf?"

"Yes. I was glad you knew how to put her there. Those statements do not amend your certificate."

"Understood."

"And if she sails again, neither gratitude nor damage restores your unilateral control."

"Understood."

The repetition did not feel submissive. It felt like a new arrangement settling under load.

At 19:22 the crew committee met by mixed presence and video from Lotte's hospital room. They voted to preserve wage escrow, appoint Els acting master for salvage administration, authorize emergency environmental expenditure, and obtain independent repair and constructive-total-loss estimates. Gabriel abstained from the vote on owner distributions and supported the rest. Lotte participated for nine minutes, then the nurse ended the call.

The committee also authorized Gabriel to remain as technical representative during the tribunal, subject to counsel. No one thanked him for wrecking their livelihood. Tomasz said the grounding had been the least bad option and that he still believed evacuation should have begun earlier. His dissent entered the minutes.

Night brought another streak of rain. Gabriel slept in the mess for forty minutes and woke when the hull shifted half a degree on the falling tide. Pumps remained stable. Shore lines held. Salvage lights made the wet deck glaze silver.

Anthea messaged at 21:10 from Athens. The certified package had entered joint Greek conference and judicial custody. Its seals were intact. Minister Anagnostou's office scheduled a closed caucus briefing for Mira on Day Forty, provided she arrived. The evidence had left by patrol launch and aircraft; the operational copies had left among Pawlu's fish crates. None of it depended on `Nkem` refloating.

Gabriel read the message twice. For years he had treated carriage as power. A thing mattered because his ship could carry it and he could decide where it went. Today the proof had passed from court officer to patrol coxswain to courier to fisherman to aircraft while his vessel remained pinned to sand. The chain was stronger for not belonging to him.

He went to the bridge. The controls were dead except for emergency instruments. On the chart, Els had marked the grounding track in pencil, preserving every amendment and uncertainty. The line did not look heroic. It looked like a short, desperate deviation away from rock.

At 22:03 Maltese police served notice that Gabriel must appear at the maritime tribunal the next morning. Bail would be considered in relation to the infrastructure inquiry, unauthorized handling under suspension, and departure risk. His passport, already controlled under earlier proceedings, remained held. `Nkem` could not sail even if repaired until released by harbor and tribunal orders.

He signed receipt.

From the doorway, Marcin asked, "Do you regret the shelf?"

"No."

"Do you regret coming?"

Gabriel contemplated the cable station, the sabotaged fuel, Lotte's broken wrist, and the ship breathing against sand. "Regret is not a casualty report."

"That is not an answer."

"Then yes. Parts of it. Not the decision."

Marcin nodded, satisfied by neither reconciliation nor despair.

The wind moved offshore before midnight. For the first time since dawn, the coast ceased to be a lee shore. `Nkem` remained where Gabriel had put her, damaged and upright. He no longer mistook saving the ship for saving what the ship had made possible.

Athens had the evidence. His crew had their lives. The vessel would face survey without his sentiment entered as a valuation.

In the morning he would face the law without surrendering the truth to obtain mercy.

## Chapter 35: Sanctuary

The parish hall offered sanctuary in the form of a mop.

At 06:18 on Day Forty, Elena stood beside a stack of folding beds while rainwater crept under the street door. The hall belonged to the Parish of Saint Paul Outside the Walls, though the name had outgrown the modern building and its gymnasium floor. Volunteers had opened it overnight for the inspection team, three families displaced by a blackout in an apartment block, two elderly tourists whose hotel lift had failed, and a night-shift nurse unable to cross a police cordon. No one had been asked what political doctrine they endorsed before receiving dry sheets.

Sister Agatha Micallef, who ran the parish charity office without being an abbess or behaving like anyone's protege, pointed Elena toward a bucket.

"The drain backs up when the wind is northeast," she said. "Push the water there, not into the cupboard. Breakfast at seven. Tribunal transport at eight. Journalists are not permitted. Lawyers are permitted if they carry chairs afterward."

Elena took the mop.

Her lower back ached from four hours on a camp bed. She remained on administrative leave, removed as counsel in Marseille, separately represented in her disciplinary case, and prohibited by good sense as well as role from litigating Gabriel's bail. Daniel Mifsud and Yasmine Aouragh would appear for him. Anaïs Roche represented the clinic interests connected to Convergence. Elena was a fact witness regarding Section 18.4 and the remote inspection. The categories had not dissolved merely because everyone slept in one hall.

Around her, volunteers moved with practical attention. A retired teacher recorded names only for fire safety and dietary needs. Two members of the laity prepared gruel for a child with a stomach illness and pastizzi for anyone able to digest pastry. A parish nurse checked Lotte's discharge plan by telephone. A man Elena had seen serving coffee the previous night repaired the leaking door seal; someone later told her he was an ex-convict who had learned joinery in prison. The fact neither absolved nor defined him. It explained why he had tools.

Noor emerged from behind a screen in yesterday's clothes and sneakers, hair still damp from the hall shower. Mira sat at a trestle table scanning the Athens agenda. The authenticated notice had reached all participating delegations, but Harborlight had circulated its exercise-artifact response and footage of the cable outage. Minister Anagnostou's office would hold the caucus at 15:00. Mira's flight departed at 11:35 if Maltese release conditions lifted by ten.

"Gabriel's hearing is at nine," Noor said. "We cannot leave before we know."

"We may have to," Mira replied. "His lawyers can act without us."

Noor looked toward Elena as if the lawyer could transmute obligation into schedule.

"Mira is right," Elena said. "Attendance is not solidarity if it costs the only briefing the evidence was obtained to support. Gabriel asked you to go."

"And if prosecutors call us?"

"Then counsel addresses it. No one should abscond. No one should volunteer detention as a moral rite."

Sister Agatha set down a tray hard enough to make cups jump. "If you are discussing strategy, use the side room. People are eating."

The rebuke embarrassed Elena because it revealed how readily the group treated any available room as theirs. They carried consequence like a title and expected ordinary institutions to reorganize around it.

In the side room, Sister Agatha stated the parish terms. The hall would provide beds, food, phone charging, medication refrigeration, transport coordination, and confidential meetings. It would not host a press conference, endorse a campaign, display Noor's recordings, or be described as the Church shielding dissidents. Volunteers held different views about the Compact, Harborlight, migration, climate policy, and Maltese neutrality. The parish priest, Father Julian Spiteri, would not invoke consecrated space to obstruct a warrant. The chapel remained open for people who wished to pray; no photograph would be taken there.

"We need none of those endorsements," Elena said.

"Good. People often discover they need them after the cameras arrive."

Elena asked for two limited acts: confidential access for Gabriel's counsel before court, and transport for Lotte from hospital to the parish guest room after discharge if medically permitted. Sister Agatha agreed to ask the relevant volunteers. She did not pledge the parish to Gabriel's innocence.

This was the kind of institutional request Elena had once considered too small. She had preferred declarations, comprehensive jurisdiction, and remedies that could be cited. Yet a bed, private room, and driver could alter whether a witness testified coherently or a defendant appeared human rather than exhausted.

At 07:03 Gabriel called from police custody. His voice sounded sober and worn. He had been detained after leaving `Nkem` at 01:20 because prosecutors considered the grounded vessel a means of departure and the fuel sabotage unresolved. He had slept in an interview room, not a cell. No charge had been filed. The hearing would address conditional release, movement, and preservation orders.

"Lotte?" he asked.

Mira gave the update. No intracranial injury had appeared. Her wrist had been reduced under sedation and placed in a temporary cast; definitive orthopedic review was pending after swelling diminished. She had three sutures and a headache. The hospital would discharge her only to supervised accommodation.

"Ship?"

Noor read Els's message. Pumps held. Salvage divers would return at slack water. Repair estimates ranged from severe to ruinous because shaft alignment could not be assessed afloat. Environmental teams found no significant fuel spill.

"Evidence?" Gabriel asked.

"In Athens," Mira said.

"Then board the flight."

Noor's mouth tightened. "We heard you the first time."

"Apparently not."

The call ended when custody staff required him to confer with counsel.

At breakfast, Father Julian arrived in a rain-darkened clerical shirt. He was younger than Elena expected and looked fatigued rather than luminous. He knelt briefly in the chapel before eating toast at the same table as the volunteers. When a parishioner asked whether the church would denounce the infrastructure-terrorism allegations, he refused.

"We do not know enough," he said. "Shelter is not a verdict."

"But the cable manager says it was sabotage."

"Then she should testify, and the court should attend. My homily is not evidence."

Elena felt the mot juste lodge in memory: shelter is not a verdict. The reporting-duty clause had failed because she had tried to make legal shelter carry moral innocence. Immunity could protect action while contemporaneous disclosure preserved judgment. Vale had retained the shelter and remitted the disclosure.

At 08:12 Mifsud arrived. He had obtained a partial copy of the coastal chamber's volatile error journal. The cut command bore the contractor certificate associated with Mediterranean Recovery Systems. More important, station access records now showed that a Harborlight security credential had queried the chamber's status at 14:08, three minutes before the contractor badge opened the lock and eleven minutes before the fiber failed. The querying credential was assigned to Tomas Rell.

"Does that prove he issued the cut command?" Elena asked.

"No. It places his credential in the control chain immediately before entry. Dr. Galea says a deeper station log may record who provisioned the contractor certificate. Police opposed disclosure overnight on security grounds. The tribunal can inspect it in camera because the outage allegation supports Gabriel's detention."

"Can Galea testify?"

"She has been subpoenaed for ten. Harborlight moved to limit her to physical causation."

Mifsud spread papers on the side-room table. The prosecution theory combined three strands: the inspection team created the operational condition; `Nkem` transported or intended to transport derived evidence; Gabriel handled a vessel under certificate suspension and disobeyed Harbor Control; therefore he presented coordinated departure risk and possible involvement in infrastructure interference. Each strand contained a fact. Their combination entailed more than the facts supported.

Mifsud would not ask the tribunal to decide the entire sabotage case. He sought bail on recognizance, medical and salvage access under escort, prohibition on vessel departure, surrender of travel documents already held, and permission for the other investigators to leave commercially. He would concede Gabriel's emergency handling and preserve arguments on necessity. He would not claim the grounding absolved earlier false reports or current regulatory review.

"Where do I fit?" Elena asked.

"Nowhere unless the prosecution misstates the remote order or Section 18.4. If called, answer facts. Do not become co-counsel by posture."

The warning would once have humiliated her. Today it relieved her.

The maritime tribunal occupied a limestone building near the waterfront. Rain had stopped, but runoff still streaked the steps. Onlookers, cameras, police, port workers, and tourists formed separate knots outside. Someone had painted `NO FOREIGN SABOTEURS` on cardboard. Another sign read `WHO CUT THE CABLE?` The second question was less venomous and more dangerous.

Inside, the hearing room held the trappings of maritime authority without grandeur: a model patrol boat, a faded navy ensign, a wall clock, and binders swollen by humidity. Tribunal chair Magistrate Claire Vassallo sat with two nautical assessors. A separate infrastructure prosecutor appeared beside port counsel. Gabriel entered without handcuffs but under escort. His clothes were clean because parish volunteers had delivered a bag from the vessel; his posture showed every hour of weariness.

Elena sat behind the witness rail, not at counsel table.

The prosecutor opened with the cable outage, criminal warrants, `Nkem`'s arrival, contaminated fuel, refusal of Harbor Control's order, grounding in a protected area, and Gabriel's suspended certificate. He did not call Gabriel a terrorist. He argued that interlocking investigations justified detention until digital evidence and vessel systems were secured.

Mifsud conceded the gravity of the outage and grounding. He contrasted them. The cable was cut in a chamber 1.7 kilometers from the station while `Nkem` remained offshore with authenticated tracking and while Gabriel was aboard only after police transfer. Fuel sabotage impaired the vessel. The master accepted patrol boarding and tug assistance but refused an unsafe return order. Gabriel touched the controls only after Lotte's injury, under Els's command and necessity. The evidence had traveled by court and government courier, not aboard the ship as an escape asset.

"The prosecution's narrative is comprehensive because it joins every alarming noun," Mifsud said. "It is not therefore accurate."

The chair asked whether Gabriel would testify. On counsel's advice he gave a limited account of command succession, grounding, and present obligations. He admitted his certificate suspension, his prior false position report, and his handling of `Nkem`. He did not dress necessity as a trophy.

"Why should this tribunal trust your recognizance?" Vassallo asked.

"It should not rely on my honorable self-description," he said. "It can rely on conditions. My passport is held. The vessel cannot sail. I have appeared under every reporting order since Tangier. I surrendered logs that increased my exposure. I will remain at the parish address, attend survey and hearing under escort, and not approach control systems except when the salvage officer requests it."

"You previously falsified a report."

"Yes. That is why verification and conditions matter more than assurance."

The answer did not cleanse him. It gave the tribunal something enforceable.

At 10:11 Beatrice Galea took the witness seat. She described the inspection sequence, traffic migration, hardware challenge, clean signature response, stop order, external attenuation, physical cut, service-chamber entry, and recovered error journal. She distinguished the judicial challenge from the fiber failure with the patience of someone required to reiterate that adjacent systems were not identical.

Harborlight counsel objected when Mifsud asked about Rell's credential. The prosecution joined the objection on security sensitivity. The tribunal reviewed the deeper access log in camera with counsel under restriction. Elena waited in the public room and watched rain brighten the windows.

When the hearing resumed, Vassallo permitted a bounded statement. Galea could say whether any named credential queried or provisioned the cut path, not disclose unrelated topology.

"At 14:08:17," Galea said, "a security credential assigned to Tomas Rell queried live state for the southern chamber and requested contractor access availability. At 14:09:03, that credential issued an override token to Mediterranean Recovery Systems certificate `MRS-CC-19`. At 14:11:26, `MRS-CC-19` opened the chamber. At 14:18:42, the same certificate signed the compression device's armed state. At 14:21:07, the fiber severed."

The room went still.

Mifsud asked, "Can a query issue an override token without human action?"

"The security credential had to authenticate. The provisioning command then executed automatically. Whether Mr. Rell personally operated the credential requires endpoint evidence I have not seen."

"Was any inspection-team credential in that chain?"

"No."

"Could the maintenance audio challenge have issued that token?"

"No. The systems are separate."

"Did `Nkem` carry the inspection equipment to Malta?"

"No. The equipment arrived by commercial flight and was logged before the vessel left Marseille."

The cable manager had tied Rell to the cut command in the exact, limited sense the logs supported. His assigned credential provisioned the certificate that opened the chamber and armed the device. She did not testify that she saw him, that Vale ordered him, or that Noor's operation bore no collateral responsibility.

Harborlight counsel cross-examined. Credentials could be stolen. Correct. Endpoint compromise existed. Correct. The inspection schedule was known to multiple parties. Correct. Traffic had been concentrated because of the challenge. Correct. Would the cut have caused the same interruption without traffic migration? It would have caused different interruptions, possibly more severe if failover had not been prepared. Did Galea approve the inspection? Yes. Did she regret it?

"Regret is not a network state," she said.

Elena almost smiled at Gabriel's influence before realizing the phrase had developed independently among people tired of moral theater.

The prosecutor requested that Rell's credential evidence remain sealed pending search warrants. Vassallo sealed endpoint identifiers but allowed the causal times and credential assignment into the bail ruling. Police had already sought preservation from Harborlight security systems and border alerts for Rell. His current location was unknown. An arrest request remained pending judicial review; no one claimed he had fled merely because he could not be reached.

At 11:24 the tribunal ruled.

The outage evidence substantially weakened any inference that Noor, Moreau, or the vessel caused the physical cut. It supported investigation of Rell's assigned credential and the contractor chain. Gabriel's prior dishonesty, foreign ties, suspended certificate, and damaged vessel created some flight and interference risk, but those risks were defeasible by conditions. Detention was not punishment for public anger.

Gabriel was released on bail by personal recognizance and a modest cash deposit posted from his own legal reserve, not parish funds. He had to reside at the declared parish guest address, report daily, avoid command or navigation, access `Nkem` only under salvage or police supervision, and attend the casualty inquiry. His travel documents remained held. The vessel remained detained and grounded. Permission to sail was neither requested nor granted.

Mira, Noor, and Elena were free to leave Malta commercially once they completed witness undertakings. Moreau could travel after court transfer of the verification package. The tribunal expressly found no basis to treat their departure as flight.

The result was narrow enough to be durable. Bail, not exoneration. Admissible authentication, not final proof of operational intent. Rell's credential, not his body at the device. A ship preserved for inquiry, not returned to sea.

Before adjourning, Vassallo addressed the Convergence package because both sides had tried to use it without agreeing what it was. The tribunal was not deciding treaty validity or emergency policy. It found that the public certificate chain, historical timestamp, object hash, and live challenge supplied a prima facie basis to treat the sealed object as what the Malta root had signed. Harborlight could still litigate whether version 4.3 was an exercise, an approved contingency, or an operational plan. It could not dismiss the object as an unauthenticated fabrication merely because remote verification had once been incomplete.

The distinction mattered to Athens. It also imposed a duty on the court. Vassallo ordered the verification method, direct recording, station logs, and derivative object kept separable. Any party quoting the document had to identify redactions and custody. The press would receive the ruling, not the controlled plan. Malta would not become an informal publisher simply because foreign delegations wanted speed.

Harborlight counsel requested a stay pending appeal. Vassallo denied a stay of certified governmental notice but prohibited general publication for another twelve hours. Emergency officials could act on the evidence; political actors could not pretend secrecy had already vanished. Elena recognized the compromise as the kind she once would have criticized for pleasing no principle. Here it preserved both warning and adjudication.

The nautical assessors then questioned Gabriel about the environmental decision. He described the sand shelf, seagrass boundary, local fishing marks, shutdown before contact, and minor hydraulic release. He credited the environmental duty officer and Pawlu Grech by name. He did not describe the protected inlet as empty simply because no people lived there.

"Would you make the same approach again?" one assessor asked.

"With the same facts, yes. With five more minutes, I would want another sounding run and earlier transfer. With ten more, I would wait for the tug. We did not have those minutes."

"That is not remorse."

"It is not meant to be. It is an account of limitation."

The assessor entered the answer without praise. The casualty inquiry would test it against recordings and drift calculations rather than moral tone.

Outside, reporters crowded the steps. Mifsud delivered the ruling without polemics. When asked whether the Church had interceded for Gabriel, he said the parish provided accommodation and no legal surety. When asked whether the tribunal had cleared the inspection team, he said it had found no present basis to detain them and had admitted specific evidence. Elena watched him refuse every invitation to make a total victory from limited acts.

At 12:03 they returned to the parish hall. Lotte had arrived from hospital with her arm in a sling, forehead bruised and sutures visible. She moved slowly and became briefly nonplussed when volunteers applauded; Sister Agatha stopped the peals after two seconds.

"She needs quiet, water, and food," the sister said. "Not exhibiting."

Lotte accepted soup at a table near the window. Gabriel entered twenty minutes later with Mifsud. He went first to her, not the cameras waiting beyond the gate.

"Acting master?" he asked.

"Els," Lotte said. "As the committee appointed."

"Pain?"

"Prescribed and tolerable. Headache. No heroics."

"Ship?"

"Still where you left her."

The line could have been a riposte. It was merely factual.

The volunteers had prepared brunch because breakfast had become lunch. Bread, olives, cheese, fruit, and a tray of strawberry pastries filled the larder table. A baby slept in a carrier beneath the notice board. The apartment families discussed electricians, not geopolitics. A retired lifeguard organized rides to the hospital. Charity logistics had no need to appear pure. Donors had conditions; supplies ran short; personalities clashed; the thermostat failed; someone had pawned a parish van years earlier and the replacement still incurred debt. The institution remained useful because people did work inside its flaws.

That work became visible when an apartment resident arrived with insulin that had warmed during the blackout. The parish nurse checked the time, storage range, and packaging rather than assuring him from kindness. A pharmacy volunteer called the dispensing chemist and arranged a replacement pen. The spoiled medicine went into a labeled pouch for proper disposal. At the next table, a volunteer translated salvage forms for a Filipino deckhand from `Nkem` who spoke excellent English but did not know Maltese compensation procedure. No one collapsed these services into a lesson about benevolence. They were tasks with standards.

The parish accounts also imposed limits. Emergency lodging funds covered three nights. Crew accommodation after that required the ship's insurer, wage escrow, or diocesan hardship fund. Sister Agatha refused to let the insurer assume volunteers would subsidize detention while it contested coverage. She asked Gabriel's solicitor for a written payment undertaking and gave him until evening.

"Charity is not a rebate for a solvent company," she said.

Elena understood the sentence as public finance in miniature. Unpriced care did not become costless. Harborlight's relocation and emergency programs likewise made labor disappear beneath aggregate benefit. The parish preserved generosity by accounting for who could pay, who could not, and who was trying not to.

Sister Agatha brought Elena a repair estimate for the hall's door seal by mistake, thinking she was parish counsel. Elena returned it.

"I am not counsel here."

"You are the fourth lawyer in one room. This is becoming a practical distinction."

"It is."

"Good. Then carry these blankets."

Elena did.

At 12:40 Anagnostou's office warned that the Athens caucus could not move beyond 15:30. Harborlight had offered delegations an accelerated financing schedule tied to ratification, including immediate resilience grants for three coastal states and carrier guarantees before the storm. Delay now had a price denominated in pumps, shelters, and payroll. The certified evidence might establish a concealed plan, but it did not answer what governments should use instead.

Mira's flight would land at 14:05, leaving little margin. Moreau's court transfer was complete. Noor's witness undertaking was signed. Elena needed one final prosecutor interview because Section 18.4 appeared in the station's deferred-reporting configuration. Her own flight seat was held for 13:10; missing it would keep her in Malta until evening.

"Go without me if necessary," she told Mira.

"Your evidence matters."

"My physical presence may not. The certified statement and challenge package are there. The caucus needs your alternative, not my authorship performed again."

Mira looked tired enough to be ill. "I do not have an alternative. I have principles and one plant repair."

"Then state that honestly and ask for time to build one."

"Why would states in extremity grant time to an investigator who cannot route an ambulance?"

"Because the signed plan makes hidden governance present danger. Because Harborlight's money is not neutral. And because you are no longer asking them to abstain forever. Ask for forty-eight hours and a test."

The suggestion was procedural, almost banal. It also required Mira to assume responsibility for failure rather than confine herself to detection.

At 12:56 the prosecutor interviewed Elena in the parish side room with her own lawyer on video. He asked why Section 18.4 used "contemporaneous" without a fixed number of minutes. She explained that emergencies varied and rigid clocks could defeat legitimate rescue. The drafting history showed repeated refusal of six-hour deferred reporting for operational sensitivity. The Convergence configuration therefore did not merely exploit ambiguity; it contradicted the negotiated purpose as she understood it. She admitted that she had accepted broad immunity language because Vale assured her no protected contractor act would alter an input later represented as independent observation.

"Do you ascribe the cable cut to Mr. Vale?" the prosecutor asked.

"No. Rell's assigned credential provisioned the cut path. I have no evidence Vale ordered, knew of, or ratified this act."

"Do you ascribe Convergence approval to him?"

"Executive architecture approved version 4.3. Vale is chief architect, but masked quorum metadata does not establish which human approved. His public and private statements support knowledge of the policy reasoning. That is not the same proof."

The prosecutor asked whether she sought immunity for her cooperation.

"No. I have separate counsel and expect discipline."

She did not feel exulted. Responsibility had become ordinary enough to state without a scaffold.

The interview ended at 13:17. Her flight had closed. Mira and Noor were already en route to the airport with Moreau. Elena could catch a 17:40 commercial flight, arriving before evening delegation meetings but after the main caucus. She accepted the consequence without turning it into sacrifice.

Before Mira left, Father Julian offered the chapel for five quiet minutes. Mira declined because boarding time had become acute. Noor entered alone, not to seek an institutional blessing but to sit where no camera could follow. She emerged with the same grief she had carried in.

"Did you pray?" Elena asked before realizing the question intruded.

Noor considered. "I listened."

That answer sufficed.

At 14:02 Gabriel went under escort to `Nkem` with Els, Marcin, insurer surveyors, police, and environmental officers. He remained in Malta. Lotte stayed at the parish hall. The volunteers arranged orthopedic transport and medication refrigeration. Her injury would not dissipate because the plot had moved east.

Elena spent the afternoon helping Sister Agatha clear the hall after the apartment families returned home. She scanned no evidence and advised no client. She folded sheets, printed travel confirmations, and watched the parish office refuse two media donations conditioned on photographing the foreign "fugitives." One donor threatened withdrawal. Sister Agatha conceded that the money would have paid the door repair and refused anyway.

"You could accept and prohibit the photograph," Elena said.

"They would denounce us and we would still have their money."

"That may be defensible."

"Yes. We chose otherwise. Institutions can have prudential disagreements without one side being wicked."

The catholic breadth of the statement, in the older sense of the word, did not erase the parish's specific rites, hierarchy, and beliefs. It made room for judgment without demanding unanimity.

At 15:31 Mira messaged from Athens airport. The flight had landed late. Police escort moved them through conference traffic. Anagnostou had extended the caucus by twenty minutes but would not promise more. Harborlight delegates were already briefing states on emergency finance. The signed plan had survived challenge; political time had not stopped for it.

At 16:05 the Maltese infrastructure court issued a preservation order for Rell's Harborlight endpoint, security token history, travel records, and contractor communications. It authorized European arrest circulation for questioning on suspicion of critical-infrastructure sabotage, subject to confirmation that he controlled the credential. It did not charge Vale or decide the Convergence case. The cable cut now possessed a criminal path independent of Noor's reputation.

The same order preserved the sabotage evidence aboard `Nkem`. Preliminary repair estimates arrived: refloating and tow alone would cost more than the vessel's available reserve; shaft, propeller, stern seal, and hull work could exceed insured value. The insurer reserved rights because of unlawful interference, emergency grounding, and Gabriel's certificate status. No total-loss decision had been made.

At 17:12 Lotte asked Elena to sit with her in the quiet room. She held a paper cup in her uninjured hand. Pain had drained color from her face.

"Gabriel thinks grounding cured him of the ship," she said.

"Did he say that?"

"No. That is why I think it."

Elena resisted the invitation to treat another person's inward state as evidence. "He accepted the committee's authority in the hearing. Whether that persists is observable later."

Lotte gave a tired smile. "You have become less annoying."

"My convalescence is incomplete."

They discussed practical matters: whether Lotte could fly with the fracture, whether she should remain near the surgeon, how the crew's lodging would be paid, who could access ship accounts, and whether Ama had been told. Gabriel had called his daughter after bail and described the grounding, injury, and uncertainty. Ama had not offered absolution. She had asked whether everyone lived and whether the evidence got through.

At 17:40 Elena boarded for Athens with her fact statement and no original evidence. The aircraft lifted over the island at dusk. From above, the cable landing was invisible. `Nkem` appeared as a small dark shape near the coast, immobilized but afloat at the stern. Valletta's streets shone after rain. The parish hall could not be distinguished from other roofs.

Sanctuary had not hidden anyone from law. It had made it possible to meet law fed, rested, represented, and not displayed. The tribunal had given Gabriel bail, not freedom to sail. Galea had testified to Rell's assigned credential, not to an entire conspiracy. The parish had performed limited acts and guarded its own purpose.

Elena had once wanted institutions to declare total allegiance before trusting them. Malta had answered with narrower verbs: shelter, testify, preserve, release, restrict, repair.

Her phone entered aircraft mode before Mira's next message arrived. The caucus had begun. Five delegations were listening. None had agreed to delay.

Athens would not offer sanctuary from choice.

## Chapter 36: The Caucus

Athens gave Mira twenty-three minutes to become constructive.

At 15:07 on Day Forty, a police car carried her from the airport along a highway shimmering above hot asphalt. Noor sat beside her with the sealed receipt for Moreau's court transfer, not the evidence itself. Moreau followed in another vehicle with a Greek judicial officer. The city emerged in layers: apartment balconies, billboards, dry hills, the glacial white geometry of distant marble under a dense summer sky. A barometer advertisement above a petrol station promised accurate weather for people who had no choice about being beneath it.

The conference hotel stood near Syntagma Square behind steel barriers and flags. Delegates, interpreters, security staff, lobbyists, investigators, correspondents, and logistics contractors moved through its entrance with the purposeful hubbub of a temporary capital. Harborlight had filled the lobby screens with storm maps and financing figures. Alexandria's storm probability had reached 0.69. The Convergence readiness threshold visible in Malta was 0.72. Modeled capacity disparity remained just below its release condition. Provisional Compact authority was still false according to the morning receipt, but a participating state's request could change it before ratification.

Mira's clothes were soaked at the collar from the flight and police car. She had eaten a starchy sandwich she could not remember tasting. Her mind felt both drowsy and painfully attuned, as if every voice entered at the same amplitude.

Anagnostou's aide, Ilias Markou, met them inside security.

"The caucus began seven minutes ago," he said. "Minister Anagnostou extended your entry until fifteen thirty. You will have twelve minutes for evidence and ten for proposal, followed by questions."

"I have no authority over the court evidence," Mira said.

"Ms. Moreau presents authentication. You present hazard and remedy."

"What remedy has been described to them?"

Markou's hesitation was brief. "A forty-eight-hour delay for independent review."

"That is time, not a remedy."

"Then use your twenty-three minutes."

The caucus met not in the hotel's grand ballroom but across a covered passage in a Hellenic Parliament annex. The room had a colonnade outside and no view of the Acropolis. Five delegations sat around an oval table with Anagnostou at the head: Greece, Egypt, Croatia, Tunisia, and the Netherlands. They had been selected because each could move a different bloc and because all faced immediate coastal obligations. Observers from the Compact secretariat, European Commission, regional development bank, and Harborlight lined the wall. Vale sat among them without the theatrical ascendant posture his opponents often assigned him. He looked tired, attentive, and entirely at home.

The five states did not form a natural alliance.

Greece needed wildfire evacuation support, ferry guarantees, and island water investment. Egypt needed storm finance, hospital supplies, port continuity, and political respect for sovereignty. Tunisia needed concessional debt terms and coastal employment protection. Croatia wanted enforceable burden sharing for smaller states and feared another hortatory treaty without money. The Netherlands wanted standards strong enough to justify its contribution and controls strict enough to satisfy parliament. Free trade language mattered to carriers; public-finance language mattered to treasuries; neither phrase moved an ambulance by itself.

Anagnostou introduced Mira without decorating her. "Dr. El-Amin participated in the court-authorized Malta inspection and challenges immediate ratification. Dr. El-Amin, state the present danger and what you ask governments to do instead."

Moreau went first. In nine concise minutes she described the sealed object, matching hash, historical timestamp, valid certificate chain, fresh hardware-signed challenge, uninterrupted civilian service during verification, and separate external cable cut. She identified every limitation. Authentication showed that `HL-MED ROOT M4` signed version 4.3 while valid. It did not establish which human approved, whether every route in the controlled payload would be used, or whether the plan had converted from exercise to operation. The court package remained under joint custody.

An Egyptian legal adviser asked whether Harborlight could have signed a simulation with an operational key. Yes. A Dutch adviser asked whether the same key served live relay functions. Yes. A Croatian delegate asked whether the plan's release conditions were current. The last authorized observation showed readiness approaching thresholds but inactive. Moreau would not extrapolate beyond custody.

Then Mira spoke.

She had prepared no blooming rhetoric in the police car. She used the sequence.

Vallon showed a system able to publish a modeled contamination warning despite normal observed final water and a competent physician's timely hold. Malta showed that the same authority-fallback rule belonged to the architecture of Alexandria Convergence. The signed plan permitted local accuracy to be degraded for aggregate throughput, excluded unofficial capacity pending central verification, and counted insurer exposure, property-transition state, and political compliance in reversal cost. It cited her own sealed Alexandria triage decision as ethical precedent. She stated that conflict upfront.

"I am not asking you to reject regional coordination," she said. "I am asking you not to confer provisional or ratified authority on a concealed policy system while its emergency conversion conditions are approaching. Delay ratification for forty-eight hours. Preserve current humanitarian operations under existing state authority. Require publication of Convergence assumptions, local override rules, and reporting timing. Test a transparent routing alternative against observed capacity before the storm."

The Tunisian finance minister, Leïla Ben Youssef, leaned toward her microphone. "What alternative?"

Mira's prepared sentence dissolved.

"One we can build to a testable minimum in forty-eight hours," she said.

"That is not an alternative. It is an aspiration."

"At this moment, yes."

The admission altered attention more than confidence.

Ben Youssef opened Harborlight's financing sheet. Ratification released an initial resilience facility of 4.8 billion euros. Tunisia's tranche covered harbor drainage, two hospital cooling projects, and debt guarantees for municipal water. Delay increased interest and could trigger a currency hedge loss. Harborlight offered to bridge forty-eight hours only if the Compact proceeded on schedule.

"You ask us to incur a measurable deficiency in order to prevent a hidden risk you cannot yet quantify," she said. "We have spent years being told that skepticism is a luxury of states with fiscal room."

Mira did not depict finance as greed. "What is the forty-eight-hour exposure?"

The development-bank observer gave figures. Bridge costs, hedge movement, and contractor standby could total twenty-two million across the five states. Some loss was recoverable if ratification followed. More serious was timing: pre-positioned equipment needed legal guarantees before carriers accepted dispatch toward the storm.

"Can existing national authority cover dispatch?" Mira asked.

The Greek and Egyptian delegates said partly. Liability remained fragmented. Elena's emergency clause had been designed for exactly this gap.

Vale requested permission to respond. Anagnostou granted five minutes.

He began with what Harborlight did well. It had already moved pumps toward low-lying Greek islands, reserved cooling units for Tunisian hospitals, secured ferries for medical deployment, and identified Alexandrian routes likely to flood. Its forecasts were not universally contrived. Its financing was not an anodyne promise but contracted capital. Delay could diminish readiness at the moment storm conditions burgeoned.

"Alexandria Convergence is a contingency framework," he said. "It exists because fragmented local systems cannot interact at storm speed. Its exercise status allows conversion only under lawful authority and measurable thresholds. The Malta document has been stripped from operational safeguards and presented by investigators whose intervention coincided with a national cable outage and vessel casualty."

Noor shifted behind Mira but made no sound.

Vale continued. He did not dissemble about local accuracy. Regional routing sometimes required decisions before every local report could be verified. A false local capacity claim could divert ambulances, strand patients, and consume fuel. Identity controls existed because disasters attracted error, opportunism, and hysteria. Reversal cost prevented continual rerouting from producing chaos. Property and insurer variables, he said, estimated transport continuity and shelter durability, not human worth.

"Dr. El-Amin knows this problem," he said. "In 2024 she faced conflicting local reports and collapsing capacity. She chose aggregate survivability. Her later lack of disclosure was amiss. The decision structure was not an atrocity. It was triage."

Mira heard the old desire to argue that her case had been misrepresented. It had. Yet rebuttal alone would let Vale retain the practical ground.

"My decision was made under scarcity I did not create," she said. "It was also biased against capacity that could not enter the central format in time. I concealed my role. Your plan uses that failure as a reusable rule while Harborlight affiliates have altered insurance, maintenance, clinical capacity, and data baselines before optimization. The difference is authorship of scarcity. The similarity is why I am responsible for offering more than objection."

Vale's expression changed by no visible degree. "And where is it?"

"Not built. The minimum design is clear. Observed current capacity, assumptions published before use, local override with named responsibility, independent challenge and response, and no use of property-transition or political-compliance variables in life-safety routing. When data conflict, the system shows conflict rather than silently demoting one source."

"That will be slower."

"Yes."

"It will be vulnerable to manipulation."

"Yes. So the test must include false local reports, broken links, inaccessible transport, and delayed confirmation."

"It may route fewer people in the first hour."

"Yes. We should measure that cost against wrong destinations, excluded shelters, and overrides no one can see."

The exchange did not produce euphoria. It produced a usable disagreement.

Anagnostou turned to the delegations.

The Croatian representative, Deputy Minister Ivana Kovač, supported delay only if existing funding commitments remained ironclad. Her parliament would not accept another postponement that allowed larger states to renegotiate shares. She wanted the forty-eight-hour test embedded as a Compact condition, not left to a private investigator's discretion.

The Dutch delegate, State Secretary Pieter van Rijn, wanted source code, audit access, and an independent security review. Mira said complete source publication in forty-eight hours was impossible and potentially unsafe. A minimal model could publish code, data schemas, assumptions, test cases, and signed outputs. Security could be tested openly without pretending every vulnerability would be found.

The Egyptian deputy minister, Samir El-Hadidi, objected to Athens testing a system for Alexandria without Egyptian operational command. His tone was glacial.

"Your alternative will not treat my city as a laboratory for European rationalism," he said.

"It must not," Mira replied. "The forty-eight-hour demonstration should use a synthetic exercise here. Deployment in Alexandria would require Egyptian authority and local participants."

"You are Egyptian when biography helps and British when institutions protect you."

The personal attack had a truth adjacent to its unfairness. Mira felt pique rise and let it pass.

"I am both regardless of whether either state trusts me. That gives me no titular authority in Alexandria. Your ministry should appoint the local decision owners. My claim is narrower: do not activate a plan that excludes unofficial shelters and clinics until centrally verified, especially when those institutions carry real capacity."

El-Hadidi asked how she knew unofficial capacity existed. Mira cited the 2024 review's documented omission and current public-health infrastructure without naming protected patient data. She did not claim present shelter counts she had not observed. Professor Layla El-Amin could help identify endowment-run and religious facilities later, but Mira had not yet asked her and did not offer family access as inventory.

The Greek finance secretary placed a cost schedule on screen. Forty-eight hours could be funded if the development bank issued a temporary guarantee and states accepted a slightly reduced first tranche. Harborlight's bridge was not the only possible arrangement. It was merely the fastest. The bank observer said an alternative guarantee required unanimous consent of its emergency committee, collateral from participating states, and an upfront reserve.

Ben Youssef laughed without humor. "So the transparent alternative begins by asking indebted states for collateral."

"That is unacceptable," Kovač said.

"It is reality," the bank observer replied.

The room entered the wearisome rigmarole of public finance: commitment fees, callable capital, pari passu clauses, procurement standstill, carrier indemnity, foreign-exchange exposure, and whether delay constituted a material amendment. Mira listened because finance was not scenery around ethics. It determined which choices could exist.

Noor passed her a note: `ASK WHAT CAN BE SEPARATED.`

Mira asked.

The bank could separate immediate carrier and medical guarantees from long-term infrastructure tranches. Existing national emergency statutes could support dispatch if the Compact secretariat issued a neutral coordination letter without provisional Convergence authority. Greece and the Netherlands could provide temporary reserve against the guarantees, then seek contribution after review. Tunisia would not post new collateral. Croatia would support reserve if smaller-state shares remained fixed. Egypt could issue sovereign cover for local port and hospital movements without accepting Harborlight route control.

The solution was neither awesome nor free. It shifted short-term risk toward wealthier states and preserved urgent logistics while delaying the larger finance release. Van Rijn warned his parliament might reject exposure. Kovač said hers might reject exclusion. Anagnostou required them to state positions, not previsions of every domestic objection.

The delegates began to coalesce around a limited package:

Existing humanitarian dispatch would continue under national command. The secretariat would issue carrier coordination without activating Convergence. Greece and the Netherlands would seek temporary guarantee authority; Croatia would join subject to unchanged contribution shares. Tunisia's hedge exposure would be covered from a conference contingency reserve if ratification followed within seventy-two hours. Egypt would retain route authority and send technical observers to the test. None of this resolved long-term money.

Vale objected that separating finance from operational coordination undermined the Compact's integrated purpose. Fragmentation was the problem the agreement existed to solve.

"Integration is not identity," Anagnostou said. "We can confer financial protection without conferring concealed routing authority."

It was the first time she had spoken against his framing.

The political balance remained changeable. A pollster's overnight numbers showed broad public support for the Compact and equally broad concern about secret algorithms. Those figures were not a mandate. Coastal mayors were calling for immediate funds. Protesters outside depicted Vale as a blackguard and Mira as a foreign agent in alternating banners. Neither caricature helped ministers keep pumps running.

At 16:24 Anagnostou called a ten-minute recess. Interpreters removed headsets and rubbed their ears. Delegates formed tight groups along the colonnade. Noor joined Mira beside a potted citrus tree whose leaves had collected city dust.

"You gave him too much," Noor said.

"Which part?"

"That your decision was the same structure."

"It was similar enough that denying it would make everything else evasive."

"He made you his adherent."

"No. He tried to."

Noor looked toward the street where chants rose inaudibly through sealed glass. "The cable statement is being refracted through every faction. One says we caused the cut. Another says the outage was entirely invented. We cannot control reception."

"You knew that before I did."

"I knew it about art. I did not know it about emergency finance."

Mira drank water. Her hands trembled from hunger. Noor produced a packet of unscented crackers from her rucksack. The ordinary care nearly undid her.

"If they give forty-eight hours," Noor said, "can you build this?"

"Not alone."

"That was not the question."

"I do not know."

"Better."

Moreau approached with a message from Malta. Rell's assigned credential had provisioned the cable-cut certificate. A European arrest circulation was authorized for questioning. The evidence strengthened the claim that the outage was separate sabotage, but endpoint control remained pending. Gabriel was on bail. `Nkem` remained grounded. Lotte was stable.

Mira asked whether to introduce the update. Moreau said only if Anagnostou reopened causation. The caucus already had the tribunal ruling. New criminal details could pique political appetite without altering the remedy.

During recess, Vale came to Mira without an entourage.

"Your model will fail the first malicious local override," he said.

"Then the test should find that."

"And the delegations will return to Harborlight after losing forty-eight hours."

"Possibly."

"You are asking them to gamble with a storm to enact your penitence."

"No. I am asking them to separate urgent dispatch from a plan you did not disclose. My penitence is irrelevant unless it improves the design."

"You will discover why we made each compromise."

"Some compromises will be necessary. Concealing them is not."

Vale looked older under the annex's hard light. "Transparency can become compulsion too. A dispatcher forced to explain every uncertain judgment while people wait is not free. A minister exposed to every input may choose what cameras reward. Visibility has its own coercive effects."

The argument was invaluable because it was true.

"Then we publish assumptions and decision records at a cadence that preserves action," Mira said. "We do not livestream clinicians. We distinguish review from spectacle."

"You are already designing exceptions."

"Yes. Aboveboard."

An aide called them back before either could claim the last word.

At 16:41 the caucus resumed. Anagnostou summarized the proposed financial separation and asked each delegation whether it would support a forty-eight-hour technical stay.

Tunisia abstained pending written hedge coverage. Croatia supported with fixed burden shares. The Netherlands supported subject to emergency reserve approval. Egypt would not support a general stay but would refrain from requesting provisional authority if the test remained synthetic, Egyptian observers participated, and current dispatch continued under Egyptian command. Greece, as chair, could defer the conference vote for procedural review but risked accusations of manipulating consensus.

That made four forms of conditional assent and one abstention, not the five-delegation coalition Mira had sought.

Anagnostou asked Ben Youssef what would move Tunisia.

"Evidence that delay buys more than another report," she said. "A working route system, tested against failures relevant to states without abundant data. And written coverage of our immediate exposure."

"By when?"

"Forty-eight hours for the system. Two hours for the finance letter."

The bank observer protested that two hours was impossible.

"Then your institution's vaunted resilience cannot produce a letter while you expect our hospitals to transform overnight."

The rejoinder drew no laughter. It was too exact.

Anagnostou turned to Mira. "Define working."

Mira had been waiting for permission and now distrusted the urge to overpromise.

"A minimal routing tool that ingests observed capacity from at least three incompatible institutional sources; displays source, time, uncertainty, and conflict; permits a named local authority to challenge or override; signs every input and output for later audit; and produces routes under simulated communications loss. It must exclude property value, insurer exposure, political compliance, and projected population withdrawal from life-safety priority. It must handle at least one false local report, one inaccessible transport option, and one delayed hospital update. Results and failures are public."

"Performance standard?" Van Rijn asked.

"Compare completion time, correct destination, accessibility, reversal count, and unresolved uncertainty against Harborlight on the same synthetic exercise. No single aggregate score."

"Who builds it?"

Mira named no nonexistent team. Athens Technical University had offered lab space through an academic contact of Roche's. Priya could advise clinical capacity remotely if her institution approved. Plant and hospital schemas already existed in restricted forms but could not be copied without permission. Greek emergency technologists, Egyptian observers, accessibility specialists, dispatchers, and independent security reviewers would be needed. Code would be open. Data would be synthetic or expressly authorized.

"Who is accountable if it fails?" Anagnostou asked.

Mira felt every old instinct seek a committee.

"I am accountable for presenting the design and test honestly," she said. "Operational agencies retain command. The university controls its lab. Domain experts own their inputs. No one is made accountable for a decision they cannot make. If the model fails, I will not call the test unfair or conceal the failure."

"Will you recommend ratification if Harborlight performs better?"

"Not automatically. Performance cannot cure undisclosed governance. But I will report where it performs better and which capabilities an alternative must retain."

Vale asked to participate in the test.

Noor's chair scraped behind Mira. Anagnostou asked on what terms.

Harborlight would provide a sandboxed system, synthetic exercise interface, and technical liaison. It would not disclose unrelated proprietary code. It requested equal notice of scenarios and an independent referee. Mira agreed to equal scenario notice only after test cases were frozen and signed; neither system should tune secretly after seeing them. Harborlight's liaison could observe under the same access controls as others. No copying of the open model without recorded access.

Vale accepted with a small nod. Mira wondered whether she had just invited the ascendant system into the workshop where it could outmaneuver them. Refusing would have made the comparison a chimera.

At 17:12 Anagnostou issued her decision.

She would delay the ratification vote for forty-eight hours under conference review authority, not suspend the Compact negotiations. Current emergency finance and carrier guarantees would be separated and continued under written national commands. No participating state in the caucus would request provisional Convergence authority during the stay. The development bank and secretariat had two hours to finalize interim coverage. Egypt would appoint observers. Tunisia would join the delay upon receiving the letter. Harborlight and Mira's team would demonstrate routing systems on a frozen adversarial exercise at the end of the stay.

If Mira could not produce a working transparent alternative, Anagnostou would not promise another delay. If Harborlight concealed test access or invoked Convergence during the stay, she would move for formal suspension. The signed plan would undergo legal review in parallel.

"This is not a referendum on algorithms," Anagnostou said. "It is a test of whether regional coordination can remain effective when assumptions and local disagreement are visible. We will not choose between secret speed and abject paralysis without examining a third option."

The delegations then converted assent into text. Kovač insisted the decision say "temporary review" rather than "postponement," because her cabinet had defended the conference date as evidence that smaller states could rely on the process. Van Rijn required a ceiling on Dutch reserve exposure and a subsequent vote before any extension. El-Hadidi inserted a sentence that no synthetic result could authorize operation in Egypt. Ben Youssef struck a clause allowing the bank to subtract hedge coverage from Tunisia's first infrastructure tranche.

Mira watched diplomacy occur through amendments too crabbed for speeches and too consequential to ignore. A coalition was not five people becoming convinced by the same argument. It was five governments finding separable reasons to support one bounded act.

Anagnostou required a recorded position from each.

Greece supported review to protect the legitimacy of emergency coordination. Croatia supported because enforceability included enforceable disclosure. The Netherlands supported because authenticated hidden policy created fiscal as well as ethical risk. Egypt would refrain from provisional authority to preserve sovereign command while testing the claimed alternative. Tunisia joined after the bank chair signed interim hedge coverage from contingency revenue without reducing its allocated tranche.

None endorsed Mira personally. None condemned Harborlight as a whole. Their concurrence was enough to alter the conference sequence.

Test governance took another seventeen minutes. The university would host but not certify its own result. A referee panel would include one emergency-operations specialist nominated by Greece, one systems auditor nominated by Egypt, one accessibility representative selected jointly by civil-society observers, and one cryptographer accepted by both Harborlight and Mira. Any disagreement among referees would be published rather than averaged away. Test cases would be generated from synthetic city data, frozen at noon Day Forty-one, hashed, and disclosed to both teams simultaneously.

Harborlight asked to use its ordinary production interface. Mira objected that production connectivity might expose live systems and allow unobserved updates. They settled on an isolated instance whose software version, configuration, and model artifacts would be signed before and after the exercise. The open model would receive the same treatment. Network access would be logged. No team could ingest corrections after the freeze except through a public incident process available to both.

"And if a dangerous defect is found during the test?" Vale asked.

"It is disclosed immediately," Anagnostou said. "This is not competitive theater."

The terms made victory less likely to be clean and failure harder to embroider. Mira signed as test lead, then wrote beneath her name that operational authority remained with the exercise controller. Vale signed for Harborlight. Anagnostou signed for the conference. The referees would countersign after appointment.

The decision did not stop the storm. It created a clock.

Vale requested clarification on the stay's legal effect. Anagnostou said Greece would not supply provisional authority and the other caucus states had agreed likewise. States outside the room remained sovereign, but the political cost of unilateral activation had risen. The secretariat must preserve all readiness recommendations and report any request immediately.

El-Hadidi said Egypt's restraint depended on real dispatch continuing. Anagnostou agreed. Ben Youssef received a draft finance letter at 17:29 and marked three clauses requiring amendment. Coalition politics continued after the apparent decision because signatures, not atmosphere, moved money.

The meeting adjourned at 17:36.

In the corridor, correspondents shouted questions. Mira gave one statement beside Anagnostou, Vale, and the five delegations. She did not call the delay a victory. She described the test, current humanitarian continuity, evidence limits, and forty-eight-hour deadline. When asked whether her model would replace Harborlight, she said no model existed yet. When asked whether that admission proved the caucus a fiasco, she said the demonstration would answer what could be built and what failed.

Vale spoke next. He welcomed rigorous comparison and reiterated confidence in Harborlight. His cooperation did not withdraw his argument or make him penitent. He had acquired a new way to depict the delay as proof of openness.

At 18:04 Mira entered a conference service lift with Noor and Moreau. The lift smelled of coffee and overheated wiring. No cameras followed.

"You volunteered us for a system," Noor said.

"I volunteered myself to lead a test. You decide your role."

"Good answer. I still dislike it."

Moreau said the court package would remain with the Greek judicial liaison. She would not join the software build. Authentication had a boundary.

On the hotel mezzanine, Markou had assembled a provisional technical group: Professor Theodora Laskari from Athens Technical University, two graduate engineers, a Greek emergency dispatcher, an Egyptian health-ministry architect joining remotely, a disability-access adviser, and a security researcher. Their lab opened immediately. University counsel was preparing data and publication terms. The first task was not coding. It was defining authority, input schemas, threat cases, and what could be observed without breaching protected records.

Mira looked at the people waiting for her to begin. She had spent years preserving independence by making criticism separable from command. Now every limitation she stated would shape someone else's work, and every omission could become a route.

Her phone showed three messages.

Priya could join remotely for four hours after her shift, with hospital permission pending. Layla had replied only: `Do not build Alexandria from Athens and call it local.` Gabriel reported that salvage divers had found greater shaft damage but no tank breach. He remained in Malta. Lotte's pain was controlled. Ama had established radio contact with the crew but had not been asked to do more.

Alexandria storm probability reached 0.70.

Mira sent Layla the test terms and asked what institutions must be represented before any later local use. She sent Priya the synthetic clinical schema request without patient data. She asked Gabriel for no shipboard labor. She asked Noor whether challenge-and-response methods could help human operators verify overrides without turning the interface into her artwork.

"I will examine the problem," Noor said. "I will not decorate your dashboard."

"Agreed."

At 18:37 they left the hotel through an underground passage toward the university vehicle. Dusk gathered over the square. Protest chants undulated between buildings. A souvenir seller lowered postcards from a rack as wind rose. Above the roofs, the Acropolis caught the last gleam, less an embodiment of democracy than a structure repeatedly used to claim it.

The forty-eight hours ahead were not sanctuary, absolution, or acme. They were a test with public failure built into its terms.

Mira had asked governments to wait for something that did not exist.

Now she had to build enough of it to deserve the time.

## Chapter 37: Open Model

The first argument concerned the word *available*.

At 19:06 on Day Forty, Mira stood in a third-floor laboratory at Athens Technical University while twelve people disputed whether an empty hospital bed existed. The room had once taught control engineering. Pneumatic diagrams remained engraved on brass plaques beside newer screens, and generations of tape had left a dark adhesive line across the floor. Beyond the windows, heat hovered over the campus roofs. Inside, a wall unit belched air with insufficient vigor and then stopped.

Professor Theodora Laskari wrote three versions of the disputed field on the board: `available_beds`, `beds_staffed_now`, and `beds_accepting_this_patient`.

“One number,” said Nikos Vrettos, a postgraduate engineer in an auburn shirt. “We have forty-seven hours. We can annotate its limitations.”

Priya’s face, projected from Marseille, showed the careworn end of a hospital shift. “A bed without a nurse is furniture. A staffed bed that cannot provide oxygen is a different kind of furniture. A bed that accepts adults may not accept a child. If your integer means all three, the model will be definitive and wrong.”

Mira had promised a minimal tool. Minimality had already become contentious.

The provisional team occupied two joined teaching labs. Laskari controlled the university space and refused the flattering title of chief academician. Salma Darwish, the Egyptian health-ministry architect, joined from Cairo with two observers and authority only over the synthetic Egyptian schema. Efi Kalogirou represented disability access. Petros Yannakis, a Piraeus dispatcher, had brought a paper roster and open hostility toward interfaces designed by people who never answered an emergency call. Noor sat beside a portable recorder she had expressly disabled from saving audio until everyone consented. Security researcher Iason Tzimas watched the network. Two students, Nikos and Danae Koralli, would build the parser. An undergraduate apprentice named Kostas fetched adapters with the air of an aide-de-camp in a war nobody had declared.

Mira divided the board into four columns: source, observation time, uncertainty, authority. She did not add truth. A source could report honestly and still be stale. An authorized person could be mistaken. A measured quantity could be precise while its name concealed a differentia that mattered to life.

“Beds staffed now,” she decided. “Then capability fields and acceptance constraints remain separate. The router may derive compatibility, but it may not call incompatibility zero capacity.”

Nikos changed the schema. Priya gave an affirmative nod.

That small decision set the pedagogy for the night. They would not concoct one universal table and force every institution into it. Each source kept its own signed record. Adapters transformed records into a common proposition while preserving the original field, timestamp, and named owner. Conflict remained visible. Missing data remained missing.
